title: Value Tilt – Don’t Give Up on Your Small-Cap Value Strategy
summary: This article argues against giving up on a small-cap value investing strategy despite recent underperformance. The author, Dr. Jim Dahle, explains the rationale behind factor investing in small value stocks, including risk and behavioral biases, and presents data indicating historical long-term outperformance. He discusses why now, given the undervaluation and underperformance of small-cap value, is a good time to stick with or even implement such a tilt, cautioning that it is a long-term decision.

title: C3 AI Accelerates AI Application Development on AWS by 26X
summary: This report details how the C3 AI Platform significantly reduces the complexity and time required to develop enterprise AI applications on AWS, accelerating development by a factor of 26x. It compares using only AWS native services versus incorporating the C3 AI Platform, highlighting the platform's ability to simplify infrastructure provisioning and reduce coding needs. The report, written by an independent system integrator, showcases the C3 AI Platform's effectiveness in increasing developer productivity and speeding up deployment.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | ICE Partners With Amazon, 3M to Identify Counterfeit Coronavirus Gear
summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is partnering with companies including 3M Co., Amazon.com Inc., and Pfizer Inc. to combat the influx of counterfeit coronavirus-related medical gear. ICE's intellectual-property unit announced this collaboration to identify suspicious shipments and remove fraudulent online listings. The companies have agreed to share information and best practices with the agency to curtail the trade of counterfeit masks, tests, and other equipment.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market Reports Pandemic Revenue Gains
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market Inc. reported a 16% year-over-year gain in net sales and a 10.6% boost in comparable-store sales for Q1 2020, largely driven by increased consumer demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's net income rose to $92 million, a 64% increase, despite higher expenses due to increased worker pay, bonuses, and e-commerce fees. Sprouts' CFO noted uncertainty regarding future consumer behavior and market visibility for the remainder of 2020.

title: Shopify surges past Royal Bank for title of most valuable company in Canada
summary: Shopify Inc. has surpassed the Royal Bank of Canada to become the most valuable company in Canada, with its market capitalization exceeding $121 billion. The e-commerce firm's shares surged due to booming demand for its online selling platform during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to higher-than-expected revenue in the first quarter of 2020. Despite a net loss, the company reported an adjusted profit and is working to support businesses moving online, although analysts express concerns about its valuation.

title: Middletown battery plant to close, cutting 200 jobs
summary: Clarios, a battery assembly plant in Middletown, will close in November 2020, resulting in the loss of about 200 jobs. The company, a global leader in lead-acid automotive batteries, will keep its distribution center in Middletown open and plans to modernize its U.S. operations and streamline manufacturing. This closure highlights the shift towards electric vehicles that use lithium-ion batteries, impacting the lead-acid battery market.

title: Target in talks to boost its same-day delivery ambitions by buying pieces of startup Deliv
summary: Target is acquiring technology assets from the same-day delivery service Deliv to bolster its same-day delivery capabilities and compete with rivals like Amazon and Walmart. The acquisition focuses on Deliv's technology for pooling multiple orders and routing them efficiently, and includes hiring Deliv's CEO and a subset of its team, as Deliv is in the process of shutting down operations. This move follows Target's previous acquisition of Shipt in 2017 to enhance its fast delivery services.

title: Hello Products Takes Natural Oral Care Mainstream
summary: Hello Products, a natural oral care brand recently acquired by Colgate-Palmolive, is expanding its offerings including a new line of CBD-infused products in Ulta Beauty stores. Despite the pandemic, the company has maintained growth in sales and operations, emphasizing self-care and natural ingredients. Hello Products aims to make natural, affordable, and effective oral care accessible to a wide range of consumers, appealing especially to younger demographics with its "naturally friendly" positioning.

title: News Outlets Want More Advertisers to Act Like Burger King (Published 2020)
summary: News organizations want more advertisers to emulate Burger King, which continued to run ads near coronavirus coverage by focusing its message on contactless delivery. Many companies used "blacklisting" to avoid articles with COVID-19 related terms, costing publishers significant revenue, while Burger King saw it as an opportunity to play a role in the crisis. This practice has had a devastating effect on ad-dependent news organizations during the pandemic.

title: Amid COVID-19, an E-Commerce World Arrives
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the growth of e-commerce, with several related ETFs, including the Global X E-commerce ETF (NasdaqGM: EBIZ), reaching record highs. The article highlights how consumer behavior shifts are driving this trend and suggests that e-commerce will continue to be a significant force in retail. EBIZ is noted for its broader e-commerce ecosystem exposure compared to rivals heavily reliant on Amazon.com.

title: Amazon to pay $11M to settle security search pay claim
summary: Amazon has agreed to pay $11 million to settle a class-action lawsuit from California workers who alleged they were not paid for time spent during mandatory security searches. The lawsuit claimed Amazon violated California labor laws by not compensating hourly warehouse workers for up to 30 minutes spent on security checks after clocking out. This settlement follows similar rulings and settlements against other companies in California regarding off-the-clock security checks, highlighting the state's stringent worker protection laws.

title: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt Cut Last Ties With The Company: Report
summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt officially severed all ties with Alphabet Inc. in February 2020, ending his 19-year tenure with the company. Schmidt, who had served in various executive roles since 2001, stepped down as a technology advisor, a move that coincided with his increased involvement in government roles. His departure also came amid criticism over his dual role as an advisor to the Pentagon while Alphabet competed for the JEDI contract.

title: PepsiCo Opens Two New eCommerce Outlets
summary: PepsiCo has launched two new direct-to-consumer websites, PantryShop.com and Snacks.com, to meet increased demand for food and beverage products amid the ongoing pandemic. These platforms offer curated "pantry kits" and a wide selection of snack products, enabling shoppers to order from home with convenient shipping options. The initiative underscores PepsiCo's focus on e-commerce and digital capabilities to meet evolving consumer needs.

title: ETFs to Track Growing Trend of Online Sales
summary: The article discusses how investors can capitalize on the increasing trend of online retail sales through targeted exchange-traded fund (ETF) strategies. It highlights the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN B) for long positions in online retailers and the ProShares Decline of the Retail Store ETF (EMTY) and ProShares Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX B+) for shorting traditional brick-and-mortar stores. These ETFs offer ways to invest in the shift from physical to online shopping, which has seen significant growth, particularly during previous holiday seasons.

title: Nvidia Unveils New Data Center Chips to Speed Pace of AI
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced new Ampere graphics chips and computers for AI processing in data centers, claiming a 20x performance increase over predecessors. These new chips are designed to handle both AI training and inference tasks, a capability that will bolster Nvidia's leadership in the growing AI market. The company is selling Ampere-based computers called DGX for $199,000 each, touting their superior performance compared to traditional Intel-based server arrays.

title: Amazon Stock Benefits If AWS Is Spun Off
summary: This article discusses the potential benefits for Amazon stock if its Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud business were spun off. The author suggests that AWS, with its faster-growing revenue and better margins compared to Amazon's e-commerce operations, could be worth more as a separate entity. The article also touches upon increasing government scrutiny on large tech companies like Amazon, Google, and Facebook regarding their dominance and potential monopolistic practices.

title: Goldman Sachs: new Co-Chief Officer and Chief Technology Officer
summary: Goldman Sachs has announced the appointment of Marco Argenti as Co-Chief Information Officer and Atte Lahtiranta as Chief Technology Officer. Argenti joins from Amazon Web Services, bringing over 30 years of technology experience, while Lahtiranta, with over 20 years of experience, joins from Verizon Media Group. They will work with George Lee to advance the company's engineering strategy and deliver innovative technology and data solutions.

title: How American Express uses Big Data to transform operations
summary: American Express leverages Big Data primarily for fraud detection and enhancing customer-merchant connections. With over 110 million AmEx cards and US$1 trillion in transactions, the company uses machine learning models and Hadoop infrastructure to analyze vast data flows in milliseconds. This strategy not only protects customer finances but also helps develop apps that benefit cardholders and encourage more businesses to accept American Express.

title: Home Depot expanding paid time off, doubling overtime pay
summary: The Home Depot Inc. has expanded paid time off for hourly workers, provided additional paid time off for high-risk employees, and offered weekly bonuses and double overtime pay to support its employees during the coronavirus pandemic. These actions resulted in a pre-tax expense of approximately US $850 million for the company. The initiatives focused on ensuring the safety and well-being of associates and customers while providing essential products.

title: 21st Century Fox completes asset divestment, creates Fox Corp
summary: 21st Century Fox has created Fox Corporation as a standalone company to divest assets in anticipation of its acquisition by The Walt Disney Company. Fox Corp will house Fox broadcasting network, Fox Sports, Fox News, and Fox Business Network, with Michael Nathanson projecting a significant portion of its earnings from Fox News. The new board members include Lachlan Murdoch, Paul Ryan, Chase Carey, Roland Hernandez, and Anne Dias.

title: Tech Moves: Qualtrics exec moves to Google; NHL Seattle expands team; former Amazon exec named Bluecrew CEO; and more
summary: This article details various "Tech Moves" in the Pacific Northwest, highlighting significant personnel changes across several companies. Key appointments include a former Qualtrics EVP joining Google, an ex-Amazon executive becoming CEO of Bluecrew, and new hires for the Seattle Center Arena project and NHL Seattle. Other notable moves include board appointments, new CROs, and executive leadership roles in marketing, finance, and engineering across the tech industry.

title: FedEx, Microsoft Join Forces Against Amazon for Package Shipping
summary: FedEx Corp. and Microsoft Corp. are collaborating to offer commercial shipping customers early warnings about potential delays due to weather, traffic, and other issues, directly competing with Amazon.com Inc. This new service, called FedEx Surround, will leverage Microsoft's cloud software and AI tools to provide real-time data to improve package movement, especially for high-priority shipments. The partnership aims to provide commercial customers with logistics tools that can serve as an alternative to Amazon for both small and large retailers.

title: 8x8 moves to Oracle Cloud from AWS amid explosive growth
summary: 8x8 migrated its core XCaaS platform from AWS to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) to meet explosive growth in demand for its communication solutions in 2020. This strategic move resulted in a 25% performance increase and network savings of over 80%, while enhancing global reach and allowing 8x8 to deliver its services more efficiently to millions of users worldwide. The company also leverages Oracle's Observability and Management Platform, including Logging Analytics, to monitor its IT environment and quickly resolve issues.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise plans cuts in jobs, executive pay to temper sales slump
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) announced plans to cut costs by US$1 billion by the end of fiscal 2022, including job cuts and executive pay reductions, following a decline in sales due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company reported a 16% revenue drop to US$6 billion in the recent quarter and is implementing measures like simplifying its product portfolio and consolidating offices to recover from supply chain disruptions. CEO Antonio Neri expects sales to recover sequentially but acknowledges the uncertainty of the economic downturn.

title: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern: 'Google's a problem for everyone who sells something online'
summary: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern criticized Google for its dual role as a competitor and a major source of customer traffic, stating it's an issue for all online sellers. Kern indicated a shift in strategy for Expedia to reduce its reliance on Google and performance marketing by improving internal merchandising and customer understanding. These comments follow Expedia's quarterly earnings report where marketing expenses dropped significantly, and the company reported a major reduction in business due to COVID-19.

title: Same Old Leadership Song Lifts These Leveraged ETFs
summary: Technology sector leadership is driving the stock market's recovery from March lows, benefiting leveraged ETFs like Direxion Daily Technology Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: TECL) and Direxion Daily Dow Jones Internet Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: WEBL). TECL is a triple-leveraged play on Microsoft and Apple, while WEBL offers a similar leveraged exposure to internet giants like Amazon, Facebook, and Netflix. Both ETFs have seen significant gains and investor interest due to the strong performance of their underlying tech and internet components.

title: Amazon Prime Air Seen Surging Fivefold, Rivaling UPS
summary: Amazon's Prime Air fleet is projected to grow fivefold to 200 planes in the next seven to eight years, potentially rivaling United Parcel Service Inc. This expansion, driven by the demand for faster home delivery, includes a significant $1.5 billion facility near Cincinnati designed to accommodate up to 100 planes and 200 daily flights, which could transform Amazon's ability to offer comprehensive domestic delivery services. While some analysts initially dismissed Amazon as a limited competitor due to its lack of a central hub, the new Cincinnati facility is seen as a pivotal investment for its long-term competitive aspirations.

title: CVS Health tests self-driving vehicle prescription delivery
summary: CVS Health is partnering with Nuro, a Silicon Valley robotics company, to test self-driving vehicle prescription delivery in the Houston area beginning next month. This marks Nuro's first venture into healthcare delivery, following previous partnerships for pizza and grocery delivery. The move by CVS Health, and rival Walgreens, highlights an industry trend to expand home delivery services amid Amazon's growing influence in retail.

title: Should You Buy or Sell Costco Stock?
summary: This article analyzes whether Costco stock (COST) is a good investment, weighing its strong performance during the pandemic and formidable business model against its high valuation and low dividend yield. It discusses Costco's growth in sales and membership, its "economic moats," and challenges such as rising costs and the need to scale up e-commerce operations. The article concludes that Costco is a wonderful company, despite its high price.

title: Target closing 6 stores 'until further notice' after protests compromise the safety of employees
summary: Target announced the temporary closure of six stores across the U.S. due to safety concerns stemming from protests, updating a decision that initially affected over 200 locations with adjusted hours over the weekend. The company is committed to reopening stores as soon as it is safe and is providing support to affected employees, including pay and the option to work at other locations. Target is also sending essential supplies to heavily impacted areas and its CEO expressed support for the protests against police abuse.
